Maratha Confederacy.d: The Maratha Empire, or Maratha Confederacy, was an early modern polity that dominated much of the Indian subcontinent in the 18th century.

French Equatorial Africa.d: French Equatorial Africa was a federation of French colonies (Gabon, French Congo, Ubangi-Shari, Chad) from 1910 to 1958, administered from Brazzaville.

Arabia.d: The Arabian Peninsula, or Arabia, is a peninsula in West Asia.

Zaire (Belgium).d: The Belgian Congo was a Belgian colony in Central Africa from 1908 until independence in 1960.

Union of South Africa.d: The Union of South Africa was a British Dominion in southern Africa from 1910 to 1961, predecessor of today's Republic of South Africa.

Saudi Arabia.d: Saudi Arabia is a West Asian kingdom covering most of the Arabian Peninsula.

Umayyad Caliphate.d: The Umayyad Caliphate was the second caliphate after Muhammad's death, ruled by the Umayyad dynasty from 661 to 750.

Iran.d: Qajar Iran was the Iranian state under the Qajar dynasty, lasting from 1789 to 1925.

Libya (IT).d: Italian Libya was an Italian colony in North Africa, in the territory of modern Libya, from the Italian conquest until 1943.

Toba Wei.d: The Northern Wei, or Tuoba Wei, was a Chinese imperial dynasty (386-535) ruled by the Tuoba clan of the Xianbei.

Oirat Confederation.d: The Oirat Confederation, or Four Oirats, was a federation of Western Mongol tribes on the Mongolian Plateau.

Magadha.d: Magadha was a region and kingdom in ancient India, based in the eastern Ganges Plain.

Hunnic Empire.d: The Huns were a nomadic people active in Central Asia, the Caucasus and Eastern Europe between the 4th and 6th centuries CE.

Northern Territory (UK).d: The Northern Territory is an internal territory covering the central and central-northern parts of Australia.

Khanate of Sibir.d: The Khanate of Sibir was a Siberian Tatar state in western Siberia, founded in the late 15th century after the Golden Horde broke apart.

Karluks.d: The Karluks were a nomadic Turkic tribal confederacy in the Kara-Irtysh and Tarbagatai regions west of the Altai Mountains.

Kiikaapoi (Kickapoo).d: The Kickapoo are an Algonquian-speaking Native American people originating south of the Great Lakes, now in the United States and Mexico.

Inupiat.d: The Iñupiat are an Indigenous Alaska Native people living from Norton Sound northeast to the U.S.-Canada border.

Pakistan.d: The Dominion of Pakistan was an independent federal dominion in the British Commonwealth from 1947 to 1956.

Burmese.d: The Bamar, or Burmese, are a Tibeto-Burman-speaking ethnic group and the majority people of Myanmar.

Papuan.d: The Indigenous peoples of New Guinea, commonly called Papuans, are Melanesians of Papua New Guinea and Western New Guinea.

Turkey.d: Turkey, officially the Republic of Türkiye, is a country mainly in Anatolia in West Asia, with a smaller part in Southeast Europe.

Inuvialuit.d: The Inuvialuit, or Western Canadian Inuit, are Inuit people living in the western Canadian Arctic.

Post-Ming Warlords.d: The Southern Ming was a series of Ming rump states in southern China that resisted the Qing after 1644.

Nigeria.d: Colonial Nigeria was the British-ruled territory of Nigeria from the mid-19th century until independence in 1960.

Ukraine.d: The Ukrainian SSR, or Soviet Ukraine, was a Soviet socialist republic in Ukraine and a Soviet Union member from 1922 to 1991.

Avars.d: The Pannonian Avars were a confederation of Eurasian nomads who ruled the Carpathian Basin from the 6th to the 9th century.

Namibia.d: South West Africa was a territory under South African administration from 1915 until its independence as Namibia in 1990.

Aónikenk (Tehuelche).d: The Tehuelche, also called the Aónikenk, are an Indigenous people of eastern Patagonia in South America.

German Empire.d: The German Empire was the German state from unification in 1871 until the 1918 revolution made it a republic.

Rome (Galerius).d: The Tetrarchy was Diocletian's system dividing rule of the Roman Empire among two senior and two junior emperors, including Galerius.

Ostrogoths.d: The Ostrogoths were a Roman-era Germanic people who founded a major Gothic kingdom in Italy in the 5th and 6th centuries.

Visigoths.d: The Visigoths were a Gothic people who emerged in the Balkans in late antiquity and later founded a kingdom in Gaul and Hispania.

Sahtu Dene and Metis.d: The Sahtu, or North Slavey, are an Athabaskan-speaking Dene First Nations people living around Great Bear Lake in the Northwest Territories.

Natchez.d: The Natchez were a Native American people of the Natchez Bluffs in the Lower Mississippi Valley, near present-day Natchez, Mississippi.

Bukara Khanate.d: The Khanate of Bukhara was an Uzbek monarchy in Central Asia from 1501 to 1785, founded by the Shaybanid dynasty.

Burma.d: The Konbaung dynasty, or Third Burmese Empire, was the last dynasty to rule Burma, from 1752 to 1885.

Shoshoni.d: The Shoshone, or Newe, are an Indigenous people of the western United States divided into four major groups.

Republic of Turkey.d: Turkey, officially the Republic of Türkiye, is a country mainly in Anatolia in West Asia, founded as a republic in 1923.

Mesopotamia (GB).d: Mandatory Iraq was the British-administered Kingdom of Iraq created in 1921 after the 1920 revolt against the British Mandate of Mesopotamia.

Botswana.d: The Bechuanaland Protectorate was a British protectorate in Southern Africa from 1885 that became independent Botswana in 1966.

Nganasan.d: The Nganasans are a Samoyedic people native to the Taymyr Peninsula in northern Siberia.

Vazimba.d: The Vazimba are, according to popular belief, the first inhabitants of Madagascar.

Turkmenistan.d: Turkmenistan is a landlocked country in Central Asia bordering the Caspian Sea, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Afghanistan and Iran.

Kenya.d: The Colony and Protectorate of Kenya was a British territory in East Africa from 1920 to 1963.

Kanauj.d: The Pushyabhuti dynasty ruled Thanesar and later Kannauj in northern India in the 6th and 7th centuries, peaking under Harsha.

Vakataka.d: The Vakataka dynasty was an ancient Indian dynasty from the Deccan that arose in the mid-3rd century CE.

Khanty.d: The Khanty, or Ostyaks, are an Ob-Ugric indigenous people of western Siberia, mainly in Russia's Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug.

Tiahuanaco Empire.d: The Tiwanaku polity was a pre-Columbian state in western Bolivia centred on the southern Lake Titicaca Basin.

Assiniboin.d: The Assiniboine are an Indigenous people of the Northern Plains of North America.

Algiers.d: The Regency of Algiers was a semi-independent Ottoman province on North Africa's Barbary Coast from 1516 to 1830.

Mwenemutapa.d: The Mutapa Empire, or Mwenemutapa, was a Shona empire in the north of the Zimbabwean Plateau.

Ndé Kónitsąąíí Gokíyaa (Lipan Apache).d: The Lipan Apache are a band of Apache, a Southern Athabaskan people long living in the Southwest and Southern Plains.

Charrúa.d: The Charrúa are an Indigenous nation of the Southern Cone, mainly in present-day Uruguay with adjacent parts of Argentina and Brazil.

Palas.d: The Pala Empire was an early medieval Indian empire ruled by the Pala dynasty, centred on Bengal and Bihar.

Wabanaki (Dawnland Confederacy).d: The Wabanaki Confederacy is a union of five Eastern Algonquian nations whose name means 'People of the Dawn' or 'Dawnland'.

Huari Empire.d: The Wari, or Huari, Empire emerged around 600 CE in Peru's Ayacucho Basin and expanded over much of coastal and highland Peru.

Imperial Japan.d: The Empire of Japan was the Japanese nation-state from the Meiji Restoration in 1868 until the 1947 constitution.

Tokugawa shogunate.d: The Tokugawa, or Edo, shogunate was the military government of Japan during the Edo period, from 1603 to 1868.

Dehcho Dene.d: The Slavey, or South Slavey (Dehcho Dene), are a Dene First Nations people of Canada.

Air.d: The Sultanate of Agadez, or Aïr, was a Berber (Tuareg) kingdom centred on the city of Agadez in north-central Niger.

Paraguay.d: The Intendancy of Paraguay, or Asunción, was an administrative unit of the Spanish Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

Chernoles culture.d: The Chernoles (Black Forest) culture was an Iron Age archaeological culture of central Ukraine's forest-steppe, c. 1025-700 BC.

Papua New Guinea.d: The Indigenous peoples of New Guinea, commonly called Papuans, are Melanesians of Papua New Guinea and Western New Guinea.

Yup’ik/Cup’ik.d: The Yup'ik, or Central Alaskan Yup'ik, including the Cup'ik, are an Indigenous people of western and southwestern Alaska.

Southern Rhodesia.d: Southern Rhodesia was a landlocked, self-governing British colony in what is today Zimbabwe.

Koyukon.d: The Koyukon, or Dinaa, are an Alaska Native Athabascan people.

Coahuiltecan.d: The Coahuiltecans were a varied set of Indigenous nations in what is now northeastern Mexico and southern Texas.

Koryaks.d: The Koryaks are an Indigenous people of the Russian Far East living north of the Kamchatka Peninsula along the Bering Sea coast.

Lusatian culture.d: The Lusatian culture was a later Bronze Age and early Iron Age culture (1300-500 BC) centred on present-day Poland and neighbouring regions.

Funan.d: Funan was a group of early Indianized polities in mainland Southeast Asia, in parts of Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam, from the 1st to 7th century CE.

Urartu.d: Urartu was an Iron Age kingdom centred on the Armenian highlands between Lake Van, Lake Urmia and Lake Sevan.

Balts.d: The Balts are peoples of the eastern Baltic Sea coast who speak Baltic languages.

Sind.d: The Samma dynasty was a Sindhi Muslim dynasty that ruled the Sindh Sultanate, a medieval kingdom based in Sindh.

Thrace.d: The Thracians were an Indo-European-speaking people who inhabited large parts of Southeast Europe in ancient times.

Vietnam.d: Vietnam, officially the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam, is a country at the eastern edge of mainland Southeast Asia.

Byelarus.d: Belarus, officially the Republic of Belarus, is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.

Lozi.d: The Lozi, or Balozi, are a Bantu-speaking ethnic group of western Zambia and neighbouring countries, historically ruling Barotseland.

Armenia.d: The Kingdom of Armenia was an ancient kingdom of the Near East from 331 BC to 428 AD under the Orontid, Artaxiad and Arsacid dynasties.

Portuguese East Africa.d: Portuguese Mozambique, or Portuguese East Africa, was Mozambique under Portuguese colonial rule.

Māori.d: The Māori are the Indigenous Polynesian people of mainland New Zealand.

Congo.d: The Kingdom of Kongo was a kingdom in west-central Africa, in parts of present-day Angola and the two Congos.

Ottoman Sultanate.d: The Ottoman Empire was a state spanning Southeastern Europe, West Asia and North Africa from the 14th to the early 20th century.

Brushed Pottery culture.d: The Brushed Pottery culture was a Bronze and Iron Age archaeological culture in eastern Lithuania, Belarus and southeastern Latvia.

Diaguita.d: The Diaguita are an Indigenous people of northern Chile's Norte Chico and Argentina's Northwest.

Peoria.d: The Peoria are a Native American people, originally a member tribe of the Illinois Confederation.

Tsuu T'ina.d: The Tsuutʼina, or Tsuu Tʼina (Sarcee), are an Athabaskan First Nation now based in Alberta, Canada.

Yemen (UK).d: The Aden Protectorate was a British protectorate in southern Arabia, around the port of Aden.

Sultinate of Zanzibar.d: The Sultanate of Zanzibar was an East African Muslim state ruled by the Sultan of Zanzibar from 1856 to 1964.

Western Sahara.d: Spanish Sahara was the territory now called Western Sahara, occupied and governed by Spain from 1884 to 1976.

Illinois.d: The Illinois Confederation, or Illiniwek, was a loose alliance of about 12-13 tribes in the Mississippi River Valley.

Uganda.d: The Protectorate of Uganda was a British protectorate from 1894 to 1962.
